newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends steady, RBI dlr buying continues.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends steady, RBI dlr buying continues.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady against the dollar at 35.6975/7025 on Friday in dull trade as focus shifted to cross currencies in dealing rooms, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) continued to mop up excess dollar supply through its 'passive' dollar buying, they said.
"The RBI must have bought over $70 million today," said the chief dealer of a state-run bank.
Most of the day's trades were at 35.6975 to 35.7025.
He said attention was shifting to cross currencies which saw sharp movements in comparison to a frigid rupee-dollar rate.
The rupee has been steady at 35.70/85 range throughout this year. "What's there in rupee to make money?" asked a dealer.
He said Indian banks were allowed to take positions on cross currencies and undertake speculative buying.
"The mark moved to 1.8400 today (against the dollar) from 1.7800 a week ago," he said. He said several banks were going long on dollars against the mark.
"Even rupee dealers are getting into crosses these days."
A cross currency dealer at a foreign bank said it made sense to block the bank's overnight exposure limits against cross currencies rather than dollar.
"For every 100 points movement on dollar-mark, you can make 15 paise," he said. "There's fairly decent money to be made."
The forward dollar market was listless, dealers said.
Premiums rose on June dollars on thin trade. The rates were fairly steady. The six month annualised forward premium closed the day at 3.69 percent against 3.75 percent on Thursday.
